unlisted_practices: Introduce productive-friction prompting (rewriting assertions as questions, requesting counterarguments and limitations before conclusions) into AI-literacy components of medical training programmes.
Configure AI systems used in educational contexts to rewrite user assertions as questions before responding and to provide a counterargument or limitations pass before any affirmative conclusion.
Evaluate educational AI tools against a tolerance-adjacent benchmark for sycophancy and critical-feedback tolerance.
Assess the local feedback climate and psychological safety before implementing productive-friction AI interventions in training.
Monitor productive-friction interventions for harms such as increased anxiety, AI avoidance, and reduced help-seeking, and provide opt-out provisions.
Provide faculty development so supervisors examine their own AI interaction habits before modeling or assessing productive-friction AI use.
Shift AI literacy education in medical training from verifying AI outputs to disciplining how users frame inputs.
Use dissent logs in AI tools that record whether alternative diagnoses or limitations were surfaced and considered before a conclusion was reached.
Move journal and programme AI-use disclosure from whether AI tools were used toward how they were used.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual perspective discussing the impact of sycophantic generative AI on medical training and proposing the concept of critical-feedback tolerance (CFT).
